title: Tessaline Fab 2's edge ring: what causes it, what it cost from April to August 2026, and after how many wafers each polish unit should change the part responsible once Rev G takes it out of the full PM
domain: Machine Learning Research, General Statistics & Data Science (Interpretability: feature attribution, probing, mechanistic analysis)
task_type: Interpretability: a sort-yield loss attributed across dependent process features to the part whose wear carries it, its dose-response, and its split across the maintenance rules

sources.origin: written for this task. Tessaline Semiconductor, Fab 2, its products, tools, people and paperwork are invented; the fab is simulated wafer by wafer (weekly lot starts at a shifting product mix, a forty-step flow with six chamber steps and one deposition chamber's affinity for two polish units, dispatch around each unit's downtime, clustered random defects with a weekly drift and a particle week, the outermost zone's fallout, conditioner-disk wear at each unit's, each supplier lot's and each disk's own rate with a pad term, thinned edge dielectric that passes sort and fails burn-in, the maintenance the spec, waiver EW-118 and the floor's unscheduled swaps produced, stores issuing the oldest disk lot first, removal-rate metrology, the ring classifier, the yield team's review pulls, assembly loss and final test at the assembly house), and every record is written from that process.
